title: Offline-first sync and conflict resolution
summary: Make the local database the source of truth for the UI, queue mutations in an outbox, sync deltas with a server cursor, and resolve conflicts with an explicit policy (last-writer-wins, field-level merge, or CRDTs).
requirements: App fully usable offline for reads and writes; changes sync when back online.
Same user on multiple devices; edits may conflict.
No lost writes; idempotent replay; bounded battery and data usage.
components: Local DB (SQLite/SwiftData) observed by the UI
Outbox table of pending mutations with client-generated IDs and idempotency keys
Sync engine: push outbox, pull changes since cursor, apply in a transaction
Server change log with monotonically increasing sequence numbers (the cursor)
Triggers: app foreground, connectivity change (NWPathMonitor), silent push, BGAppRefresh
tradeoffs: Last-writer-wins (by server timestamp) is simple but silently drops concurrent edits.
Field-level merge keeps non-overlapping edits; true conflicts still need a rule or user prompt.
CRDTs (e.g. for text or lists) merge automatically without coordination but add metadata size and complexity.
Operation-based sync (send intents like 'add item') merges better than state-based (send whole objects) but needs server logic per operation.
Full resync is a safe fallback when the cursor is too old or the schema changed, but costs data.
body: **Write path:** UI writes to the local DB and the outbox in one transaction (optimistic update). The sync engine sends outbox entries in order with idempotency keys; on success marks them done and stores server versions; on permanent failure (validation), rolls back the local change and informs the user.

**Read path:** `GET /changes?cursor=X` returns upserts and tombstones (deletes) plus a new cursor. Apply in a transaction, skipping entities with pending local mutations or rebasing those mutations on top.
**Conflict detection:** each entity carries a version (server-incremented). The client sends `baseVersion`; the server rejects or merges if the current version differs.
**IDs:** client-generated UUIDs (or UUIDv7 for ordering) avoid temp-ID remapping.

**Edge cases:** clock skew (never trust device time for ordering), app killed mid-sync (transactions + idempotency), schema migration while outbox has old-format entries, user logs out with unsynced changes (warn), very long offline periods (cursor expired → full resync).
**Apple stack option:** CloudKit with `CKSyncEngine` (iOS 17) handles change tokens, batching and scheduling; you still define conflict resolution.
**Staff angle:** sync is a platform used by many features. Provide a generic engine with per-entity conflict policies, metrics (outbox depth, sync latency, conflict rate), and a debug screen.
